overview: This Senate resolution honors the life of Frederick W. Smith, the founder of FedEx, following his death. It describes his upbringing in Memphis, Tennessee, his service as a Marine officer in the Vietnam War, where he earned the Silver Star, Bronze Star and two Purple Hearts, and his founding of Federal Express, which grew from 14 jets into a global shipping and logistics company. It also recognizes his charitable work and his dedication to Memphis. The resolution asks that it be shared with the House and that a formal copy be sent to his family. The Senate agreed to it on June 26, 2025.
for: Supporters say it fittingly honors a decorated veteran and entrepreneur who transformed package delivery and invested in his community.
against: Critics say it is symbolic and does not change any law or spending.
